traps: 📄 Built from the SLIDES only (lecture Thu 11/12) — stars and corrections update when the transcript arrives.
CHOANA = the CAUDAL opening of the nasal cavity (into the nasopharynx) vs bony nasal APERTURE = the ROSTRAL opening (slide 5) vs CONCHAE = bony scrolls inside the cavity (slide 11). Choana ≠ concha.

Dorsal nasal concha = ethmoid crest of the NASAL bone, 1st ENDOturbinate, LONGEST. Ventral nasal concha = conchal crest of the MAXILLA, P1–P3, forms the ALAR fold. Middle (ethmoidal) concha = 2nd ENDOturbinate (slides 14–16).
ENDOturbinates (I–IV, Roman) project into the NASAL CAVITY; ECTOturbinates (1–6, Arabic) project into the FRONTAL SINUS (slide 17).
Meatus ↔ destination (slide 18): dorsal → nasal cavity (as written); MIDDLE → paranasal SINUSES; VENTRAL → PHARYNX; common = beside the septum. Middle = sinuses, ventral = pharynx — don't flip.
Figure numbering flips between figures: Fig 04-03A (slide 11) 1 = DORSAL concha, 2 = VENTRAL; Fig 04-02 (slides 12–13) 2 = VENTRAL, 3 = DORSAL. Read the legend each time.
Laryngeal cavity order rostral → caudal: laryngeal inlet → VESTIBULE → vestibular fold → GLOTTIS / rima glottidis (glottic cleft) → INFRAGLOTTIC cavity → trachea (slides 33–34).
VESTIBULAR fold (rostral, bounds the vestibule) vs VOCAL fold (caudal, contains the vocal ligament + vocalis m.); the laryngeal VENTRICLE sits between them (slide 34).
Only ONE laryngeal muscle on the slides is innervated by the CRANIAL laryngeal nerve: cricothyroideus (tenses the vocal fold). All the others = CAUDAL laryngeal nerve (slides 39–43).
Cricoarytenoideus DORSALIS = the MAIN ABDUCTOR = OPENS the glottis. Cricoarytenoideus LATERALIS = narrows/CLOSES the glottic cleft (slides 40–41). Dorsal opens, lateral closes.
Thyroarytenoideus splits: VENTRICULARIS (rostral division, constricts glottis, DILATES the ventricle) vs VOCALIS (medial division, inside the vocal fold, RELAXES the vocal fold) (slide 42).

⚠️ FLAG (slide 31 vs slide 40): cricoid figure labels the 'MEDIAN crest'; the cricoarytenoideus dorsalis origin says 'lateral to the MEDIAL crest'. Same structure, two spellings — confirm which term to write (median vs medial).

⚠️ FLAG (slide 18): 'Dorsal nasal meatus – communicates with nasal cavity' — every meatus is part of the nasal cavity, so this is uninformative as written. Standard anatomy: dorsal meatus leads to the olfactory (ethmoidal) region (outside knowledge — confirm in transcript).

⚠️ FLAG (slide 25 vs slide 28): slide 25 says the epiglottis tilts backward 'to cover the opening of larynx'; slide 28 says it 'PARTIALLY cover[s] the rostral opening'. Use 'partially' (the more specific statement) until the transcript confirms.

⚠️ FLAG (slide 20 vs slide 22): slide 20 lists 'Maxillary recess (sinus)' among paranasal sinuses (diverticula between bone laminae), but slide 22 defines it as a diverticulum of the NASAL CAVITY. Use 'maxillary recess' as the name.

items.q: Learning objectives for Lecture 33, Respiratory Components of the Head (slide 2)…
items.a: 1. Describe and compare the features of the NOSE; 2. Describe and compare the features of the LARYNX

items.q: Kahoot (in-class quiz) breaks in this deck — which slides?
items.a: Slides 4, 19, 27, 38 (after nose overview, after meatuses, after the cartilage list, after the muscle overview)

items.q: Where does the nose section (LO1) run, and where does the larynx section (LO2) run?
items.a: LO1 nose = slides 3–23; LO2 larynx = slides 24–45

items.q: Airflow path from the nostril to the trachea, using structures on slides 12, 18, 25, 34…
items.a: Nostril (naris) → nasal vestibule → nasal cavity (meatuses between the conchae; ventral meatus leads to the pharynx) → choana → nasopharynx → laryngopharynx → laryngeal inlet → vestibule → glottis (rima glottidis) → infraglottic cavity → trachea
items.why: Pathway built across LO1 + LO2 figures (slides 12, 18, 25, 34)

items.q: The nose consists of… (slide 3)
items.a: External NARES and their CARTILAGES; nasal cavity and its MEATI and CONCHAE; PARANASAL SINUSES (encased in a bony case)

items.q: Dorsal boundary of the nasal cavity (slide 5)?
items.a: Nasal bones

items.q: Lateral boundary of the nasal cavity (slide 5)?
items.a: Maxilla and incisive bone

items.q: Ventral boundary of the nasal cavity (slide 5)?
items.a: Maxilla (palatine process) and palatine bone (horizontal lamina)

items.q: Caudal boundary of the nasal cavity (slide 5)?
items.a: Cribriform plate (ethmoid bone)

items.q: Bony nasal aperture (slide 5)?
items.a: The ROSTRAL opening; rostrally bounded by the nasal cartilages and their ligaments

items.q: Choana (slide 5)?
items.a: The CAUDAL opening of the nasal cavity (into the nasopharynx)

items.q: Nares (nostrils) — 3 features on slide 6…
items.a: Form the muzzle; nasal plate divided by a groove (philtrum); supported by cartilages

items.q: Philtrum (slide 6)?
items.a: The median groove dividing the nasal plate

items.q: Color of the nasal plate is related to… (slide 7)
items.a: Color of the fur (cat photo comparison)

items.q: Nasal cartilages listed (slide 8)…
items.a: Nasal septum (cartilage); lateral nasal cartilages (dorsal and ventral)

items.q: Function of the cartilaginous nasal septum (slide 8)?
items.a: Divides the nasal cavity into left and right

items.q: Function of the lateral nasal cartilages (slide 8)?
items.a: Determine the form of the opening of the nostril; dorsal and ventral lateral nasal cartilages contact each other

items.q: Cartilages labeled on the nostril figure (slide 8)…
items.a: Cartilaginous septum, dorsal lateral nasal cartilage, ventral lateral nasal cartilage, accessory cartilage

items.q: Extent of the nasal cavity (slide 9)?
items.a: From the NOSTRILS to the CRIBRIFORM PLATE of the ethmoid bone

items.q: What divides the nasal cavity into left and right (slide 9)?
items.a: Nasal septum

items.q: What projects into the nasal cavity (slide 9)?
items.a: Conchae

items.q: Four portions of the nasal septum, as listed (slide 10)…
items.a: Osseous portion; cartilaginous portion (caudal); membranous portion; cartilaginous portion (rostral)

items.q: Order of the septum portions caudal → rostral on the figure (slide 10)…
items.a: Osseous septum → cartilaginous septum → membranous septum → cartilaginous septum (rostral, by the incisive bone)

items.q: Bones labeled around the nasal septum figure (slide 10)…
items.a: Ethmoid bone, frontal bone, nasal bone, maxilla, incisive bone, palatine bone, hard palate (+ nasopharynx)

items.q: Conchae — definition (slide 11)?
items.a: Bony scrolls covered with nasal mucosa

items.q: Three conchae (slide 11)…
items.a: 1. Dorsal concha; 2. ventral concha; 3. middle (ethmoidal) concha

items.q: Fig 04-03A legend, transverse section of the dog head at P2 (slide 11)…
items.a: 1 dorsal concha; 2 ventral concha; 2′ recess of ventral concha; 3 nasal septum; 4 hard palate; 5 venous plexus in nasal mucosa; 6 tongue

items.q: Fig 04-02 legend, paramedian section of the dog head (slides 12–13)…
items.a: 1 right nostril; 2 ventral nasal concha; 3 dorsal nasal concha; 4 ethmoidal conchae; 5 frontal sinus; 6 hard palate; 7 vomer (resected); 8 tongue; 8′ oropharynx; 9 soft palate; 9′ nasopharynx; 10 epiglottis; 11 basihyoid; 12 trachea; 13 esophagus
items.why: Numbered figure, enlarged on slide 13 ('Goal #1: Nose')

items.q: Dorsal nasal concha — origin (slide 14)?
items.a: Ethmoid crest of the NASAL bone

items.q: Dorsal nasal concha — extent (slide 14)?
items.a: From the cribriform plate to the nasal vestibule

items.q: Dorsal nasal concha is formed by… (slide 14)
items.a: The FIRST endoturbinate

items.q: Longest concha in the domestic mammals (slide 14)?
items.a: Dorsal nasal concha

items.q: Ventral nasal concha — origin (slide 15)?
items.a: Conchal crest of the MAXILLA

items.q: Ventral nasal concha — extent (slide 15)?
items.a: From the first premolar tooth (P1) to the third premolar tooth (P3)

items.q: Ventral nasal concha folds unite rostrally to form… (slide 15)
items.a: The ALAR FOLD (from many longitudinal folds)

items.q: Middle (ethmoidal) nasal concha — 3 features (slide 16)…
items.a: Fills the caudal part of the nasal cavity; formed by the SECOND endoturbinate; part of the ethmoidal labyrinth

items.q: Ethmoidal labyrinth — definition (slide 17)?
items.a: Outgrowths of the ethmoid bone, covered with nasal mucosa

items.q: Endoturbinates — numbering and where they project (slide 17)?
items.a: Endoturbinates I–IV → NASAL CAVITY

items.q: Ectoturbinates — numbering and where they project (slide 17)?
items.a: Ectoturbinates 1–6 → FRONTAL SINUS

items.q: All ethmoturbinates attach to… (slide 17)
items.a: The external lamina and the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone

items.q: Which endoturbinate forms the dorsal concha? The middle concha?
items.a: Dorsal = 1st endoturbinate (slide 14); middle (ethmoidal) = 2nd endoturbinate (slide 16)

items.q: Meatuses (meati) — definition (slide 18)?
items.a: Clefts in the nasal cavity created by the conchae

items.q: Four nasal meatuses (slide 18)…
items.a: 1. Dorsal; 2. middle; 3. ventral; 4. common nasal meatus

items.q: Dorsal nasal meatus — per slide 18?
items.a: Communicates with the nasal cavity (see ⚠️ flag — outside knowledge: leads to the olfactory region)

items.q: Middle nasal meatus communicates with… (slide 18)
items.a: Paranasal sinuses

items.q: Ventral nasal meatus leads to… (slide 18)
items.a: Pharynx — the main airway

items.q: Common nasal meatus — location?
items.a: Vertical space along the nasal septum, continuous with the other meatuses (figure label 4, slide 18; description is outside knowledge — confirm)

items.q: Fig 04-05 legend — which species and level (slide 18)?
items.a: EQUINE head, transverse section at P4: 1 nasal septum; 2 dorsal concha; 3 ventral concha; 4 common meatus; 5 dorsal meatus; 6 middle meatus; 7 ventral meatus; 8 venous plexus in nasal mucosa

items.q: Paranasal sinuses — definition (slide 20)?
items.a: Air-filled diverticula between the external and internal lamina of skull bones, lined by respiratory mucosa

items.q: Four paranasal sinuses listed (slide 20)…
items.a: 1. Maxillary recess (sinus); 2. frontal sinus; 3. palatine sinus; 4. sphenoidal sinus

items.q: Labels on the dorsal-view skull figure, Nickel fig. 293 (slide 21)…
items.a: Lateral frontal sinus (b), medial frontal sinus (c), rostral frontal sinus (d), maxillary recess (a)

items.q: Maxillary recess — 4 features (slide 22)…
items.a: Only in DOGS AND CATS; diverticulum of the NASAL CAVITY; at the level of the MIDDLE nasal concha; does NOT increase in size with age

items.q: Fig 04-06 (slides 22–23): 1 vs 2?
items.a: 1 = maxillary recess; 2 = frontal sinus

items.q: Frontal sinus — location (slide 23)?
items.a: Rostral two-thirds of the frontal bone

items.q: Three frontal sinus compartments and their size (slide 23)…
items.a: 1. Lateral — LARGEST; 2. medial — small; 3. rostral

items.q: Do the frontal sinus compartments communicate (slide 23)?
items.a: NO — the three compartments do not communicate with each other

items.q: How does each frontal sinus compartment drain (slide 23)?
items.a: Opens separately into the nasal cavity via the space between the 2nd and 3rd ECTOturbinates

items.q: Clinical relevance of non-communicating frontal compartments?
items.a: Each must be addressed separately (e.g., trephination/drainage of sinusitis) (outside knowledge — confirm)

items.q: Larynx — functions/features (slide 24)…
items.a: Connects pharynx to trachea; prevents aspiration of foreign material into the lower respiratory tract; vocalization; walls formed by cartilages + their muscles and ligaments; joins the hyoid apparatus rostrally and trachea caudally

items.q: What happens to the epiglottis during swallowing (slides 25, 28)?
items.a: Tilts backward to (partially) cover the opening (rostral opening/inlet) of the larynx

items.q: The larynx is caudally continuous with… (slide 25)
items.a: Lumen of the trachea

items.q: Fig 03-27 legend, pharynx schematic (slide 25)…
items.a: 1 nasal cavity; 2 oral cavity; 3 soft palate; 4 nasopharynx; 5 root of tongue; 6 larynx (protruding through pharyngeal floor); 7 laryngopharynx (piriform recess); 8 caudal end of palatopharyngeal arch; 9 esophagus; 10 lamina of cricoid cartilage; 11 trachea

items.q: In Fig 03-27, broken arrow vs single arrow (slide 25)?
items.a: Broken arrow = FOOD passage; single arrow = AIR passage

items.q: Where does food cross the airway (slide 25)?
items.a: In the pharynx — food passes around the larynx through the laryngopharynx (piriform recess) to the esophagus

items.q: Four laryngeal cartilages (slide 26)…
items.a: 1. Epiglottis; 2. arytenoid; 3. cricoid; 4. thyroid

items.q: Which laryngeal cartilage is paired?
items.a: Arytenoid (outside knowledge — confirm; slide 35 refers to 'the two arytenoid cartilages')

items.q: What do numbers 46–56 on slide 26 (Budras p. 101) mark?
items.a: No legend on the slide — Budras cartilage figure numbers; wait for transcript

items.q: Epiglottis — position (slide 28)?
items.a: MOST ROSTRAL laryngeal cartilage

items.q: Three parts of the epiglottis (slide 28)…
items.a: 1. Apex; 2. base; 3. stalk

items.q: Epiglottic apex — 2 features (slide 28)?
items.a: Points rostrally; SHARP POINTED in dogs

items.q: Epiglottis is connected to… (slide 28)
items.a: The thyroid cartilage (via the stalk; thyroepiglottic ligament, slide 35)

items.q: Thyroid cartilage labels, lateral view (slide 29)…
items.a: Rostral cornu, caudal cornu, rostral thyroid notch, oblique line, caudal thyroid notch, lamina

items.q: Thyroid cartilage, ventral view legend (slide 30)…
items.a: 1 junction of laminae; 2 lamina; 3 rostral cornu; 4 caudal cornu; 5 caudal thyroid notch; 7 laryngeal prominence

items.q: Laryngeal prominence (slide 30)?
items.a: Ventral bulge at the junction of the thyroid laminae (label 7)

items.q: Cricoid cartilage labels (slide 31)…
items.a: Median crest, lamina, cricoarytenoid articulation, cricothyroid articulation, arch

items.q: Cricoid: which part is dorsal, which is ventral?
items.a: Lamina = dorsal (with the median crest); arch = ventral (outside knowledge — confirm; slide 31 figure)

items.q: Cricoid articulates with which two cartilages (slide 31)?
items.a: Arytenoid (cricoarytenoid articulation) and thyroid (cricothyroid articulation)

items.q: Four processes of the arytenoid cartilage (slide 32)…
items.a: Corniculate process, cuneiform process, muscular process, vocal process

items.q: Which arytenoid process do most intrinsic muscles insert on (slides 40–43)?
items.a: Muscular process

items.q: Which arytenoid process anchors the vocal fold (slides 32, 42)?
items.a: Vocal process

items.q: Three transverse segments of the laryngeal cavity, rostral → caudal (slide 33)…
items.a: 1. Vestibule; 2. glottic cleft (rima glottidis); 3. infraglottic cavity

items.q: Vestibule — position and extent (slide 33)?
items.a: Rostral to the glottis; extends from the LARYNGEAL INLET to the VESTIBULAR FOLD

items.q: Glottic cleft / rima glottidis (slide 33)?
items.a: The middle, narrow portion of the laryngeal cavity

items.q: Infraglottic cavity (slide 33)?
items.a: Caudal to the glottis (continues into the trachea)

items.q: Labels on the laryngeal cavity figure (slide 34)…
items.a: Laryngeal inlet, aryepiglottic fold, laryngeal ventricle, vestibular fold, vocal fold, vestibule, glottic cleft/glottis, infraglottic cavity

items.q: Which fold is rostral — vestibular or vocal (slide 34)?
items.a: Vestibular fold is rostral; vocal fold is caudal; the laryngeal ventricle lies between them

items.q: Aryepiglottic fold (slide 34)?
items.a: Fold from the arytenoid to the epiglottis forming the side of the laryngeal inlet

items.q: Cartilage letters on the laryngeal figures (slides 34, 36)…
items.a: A epiglottic; B arytenoid; C thyroid; D cricoid; E trachea

items.q: Seven laryngeal ligaments listed (slide 35)…
items.a: Cricotracheal lig.; cricothyroid lig.; dorsal cricoarytenoid lig.; transverse arytenoid lig.; thyrohyoid membrane; thyroepiglottic lig.; hyoepiglottic lig.

items.q: Which two ligaments are underlined on slide 35 (and green-highlighted on slide 36)?
items.a: Cricotracheal ligament and cricothyroid ligament

items.q: Cricotracheal ligament connects…
items.a: Cricoid cartilage ↔ trachea (name-based; slide 36 figure)

items.q: Cricothyroid ligament connects…
items.a: Cricoid ↔ thyroid cartilage (ventral, slide 36)

items.q: Transverse arytenoid ligament (slide 35)?
items.a: Connects the dorsocaudal angles of the two arytenoid cartilages

items.q: Which membrane does the cranial laryngeal artery perforate (slides 35, 44)?
items.a: Thyrohyoid membrane

items.q: Other labels on the ligament figure, Budras p. 106 (slide 36)…
items.a: Dorsal cricoarytenoid lig., hyoepiglottic lig., basihyoid, thyrohyoid membrane, vestibular lig., vocal lig., laryngeal fibroelastic membrane

items.q: Ligament inside the vocal fold (slides 36, 42)?
items.a: Vocal ligament (with the vocalis muscle)

items.q: Extrinsic laryngeal muscles — definition + 4 names (slide 37)…
items.a: Connect the larynx with the hyoid bone, pharynx and sternum: 1. thyrohyoideus; 2. sternothyroideus; 3. thyropharyngeus; 4. cricopharyngeus

items.q: Intrinsic laryngeal muscles — definition + 2 functions (slide 37)…
items.a: Pass from one cartilage to another and move them relative to one another; WIDEN and NARROW the glottic cleft; TENSE and RELAX the vocal fold

items.q: Cricothyroideus — origin, insertion, action, innervation (slide 39)?
items.a: O: cricoid arch (lateral surface); I: thyroid cartilage (caudal cornu, lateral surface); A: TENSES the vocal fold; N: CRANIAL laryngeal nerve

items.q: Cricoarytenoideus dorsalis — origin, insertion, action, innervation (slide 40)?
items.a: O: cricoid cartilage (lateral to the medial crest); I: arytenoid cartilage (muscular process); A: MAIN ABDUCTOR of the arytenoid — opens the glottis, widens the glottic cleft; N: caudal laryngeal nerve
items.why: Red name + purple 'main abductor' + orange nerve (slide 40)

items.q: Main abductor of the arytenoid cartilage (slide 40)?
items.a: Cricoarytenoideus dorsalis

items.q: Clinical correlation of the main abductor?
items.a: Laryngeal paralysis — loss of cricoarytenoideus dorsalis function (caudal/recurrent laryngeal nerve) → arytenoid can't abduct → inspiratory stridor (outside knowledge — confirm)

items.q: Cricoarytenoideus lateralis — origin, insertion, action, innervation (slide 41)?
items.a: O: cricoid cartilage (lateral and rostral surface); I: arytenoid (muscular process); A: NARROWS, CLOSES the glottic cleft; N: caudal laryngeal nerve

items.q: Thyroarytenoideus — origin, insertion, action, innervation (slide 42)?
items.a: O: thyroid cartilage (internal midline); I: arytenoid (muscular process and vocal process); A: RELAXES the vocal fold, constricts the glottis; N: caudal laryngeal nerve

items.q: Two divisions of the thyroarytenoideus (slide 42)…
items.a: Ventricularis (rostral) and vocalis (medial)

items.q: Ventricularis muscle — division and action (slide 42)?
items.a: ROSTRAL division; constricts the glottis, DILATES the laryngeal ventricle

items.q: Vocalis muscle — division, location, action (slide 42)?
items.a: MEDIAL division; lies inside the vocal fold with the vocal ligament; draws the arytenoid cartilage ventrally → RELAXES the vocal fold

items.q: Arytenoideus transversus — origin, insertion, action, innervation (slide 43)?
items.a: O and I: arytenoid cartilage (muscular process) — connects the muscular processes of the TWO arytenoids; A: constricts the glottis, narrowing the glottic cleft; N: caudal laryngeal nerve

items.q: Which intrinsic muscles WIDEN the glottic cleft vs NARROW it (slides 40–43)?
items.a: Widen: cricoarytenoideus dorsalis only. Narrow/constrict: cricoarytenoideus lateralis, thyroarytenoideus (incl. ventricularis), arytenoideus transversus

items.q: Which intrinsic muscle TENSES the vocal fold vs RELAXES it (slides 39, 42)?
items.a: Tenses: cricothyroideus. Relaxes: thyroarytenoideus (vocalis)

items.q: Which intrinsic muscle has origin AND insertion on the same cartilage type (slide 43)?
items.a: Arytenoideus transversus (arytenoid → arytenoid)

items.q: Main artery of the larynx (slide 44)?
items.a: Cranial laryngeal artery

items.q: Origin of the cranial laryngeal artery (slide 44)?
items.a: Direct (SECOND) branch of the external carotid artery

items.q: Course of the cranial laryngeal artery (slide 44)?
items.a: Runs ventrally with the cranial laryngeal nerve and perforates the thyrohyoid membrane

items.q: What does the cranial laryngeal artery supply (slide 44)?
items.a: Most of the mucosa and the INTRINSIC MUSCLES of the larynx

items.q: Nerve branches underlined on the innervation figure, Evans fig. 8-22 (slide 45)…
items.a: Cranial laryngeal n., its external branch, ramus anastomoticus, caudal laryngeal n.

items.q: Two branches of the cranial laryngeal nerve (slide 45)?
items.a: External branch and internal branch

items.q: Internal branch of the cranial laryngeal nerve goes to… (slide 45)
items.a: Laryngeal mucosa (and toward the epiglottis) — sensory (sensory role is outside knowledge — confirm)

items.q: External branch of the cranial laryngeal nerve supplies…
items.a: Cricothyroideus (matches slide 39; branch-to-muscle link is outside knowledge — confirm)

items.q: Ramus anastomoticus (slide 45)?
items.a: Connecting branch between the caudal laryngeal nerve and the cranial laryngeal nerve (internal branch)

items.q: Muscle branches of the caudal laryngeal nerve on slide 45…
items.a: To arytenoideus transversus & ventricularis, to cricoarytenoideus dorsalis, to cricoarytenoideus lateralis, to vocalis, to thyroarytenoideus (+ to trachea, to pharyngeal mucosa)

items.q: Caudal laryngeal nerve is the continuation of…
items.a: Recurrent laryngeal nerve of the vagus (outside knowledge — confirm)

items.q: Both laryngeal nerves come from which cranial nerve?
items.a: Vagus nerve (cranial nerve X) (outside knowledge — confirm)
